fullPassage:
Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy. Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good. On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, the analogy is supposed to show why we should conclude that the universe has a creator.

* analogy: 유추 ** theologian: 신학자 *** artisan: 장인

✅ ① 정교하게 설계된 물건이 존재하면 그것을 만든 설계자가 반드시 있다: 시계(인공물)→장인(제작자)의 유추 핵심 ← 정답

❌ ② 장인의 존재는 시계와 무관하게 독립적으로 증명된다: 유추의 핵심이 아님

❌ ③ 시계는 자연적으로 생겨난 산물이므로 장인이 필요 없다: 인공물이라는 원문과 반대

❌ ④ 고대의 시계 제작 기술이 현대보다 더 정교했다: 시계 기술 비교는 논점이 아님
det.tip: artefact→artisan = 설계물→설계자. 이 유추를 우주→창조자로 확장

ch: 정교하게 설계된 물건이 존재하면 그것을 만든 설계자가 반드시 있다.
장인의 존재는 시계와 무관하게 독립적으로 증명된다.

고대의 시계 제작 기술이 현대보다 더 정교했다.

overlay.underline: just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan

questions.passage: Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy. Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good. On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, <u>the analogy</u> is supposed to show why we should conclude that the universe has a creator.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 <u>the analogy</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 소크라테스가 선과 태양을 비교한 유추: 이 유추는 앞부분 사례이며, here에서 가리키는 것은 설계 논증의 유추

✅ ② 시계와 장인의 관계를 우주와 창조자에 적용한 유추: 바로 앞 문장의 설계 논증 유추 ← 정답

❌ ③ 플라톤이 철학에서 사용한 일반적 비유: 플라톤의 비유 전체가 아닌 특정 설계 논증

❌ ④ 윌리엄 페일리가 발명한 새로운 논증 방법: 페일리만의 발명이 아니라 고대부터 이어진 논증
det.tip: Here the analogy = 바로 앞 설계 논증의 시계-장인 유추

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Analogies can serve two different functions in philosophy.

(A) The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point.

(B) On other occasions, however, the analogy can be an integral part of an argument. Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley.

(C) Sometimes, as seems often the case in Plato, for example, they serve simply to illustrate. When Socrates compares the Good with the sun, he may simply be using the image of the sun to help bring to life his arguments about the Good.

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)-(B)-(C): 도입문 후 바로 설계 논증 세부 내용은 맥락 없음

❌ ② (A)-(C)-(B): 논리적 흐름 어색

✅ ③ (C)-(B)-(A): Sometimes(첫째 기능: 설명) → On other occasions, however(둘째 기능: 논증 핵심) → The argument holds that(설계 논증 구체 내용) ← 정답

❌ ④ (B)-(A)-(C): however로 시작하려면 대비 대상이 먼저 필요
det.tip: (C) 첫째 기능(설명) → (B) 둘째 기능(논증 핵심) → (A) 설계 논증 구체화

Consider one of the most popular arguments for the existence of God, the 'argument from design', which has been advanced by many thinkers, from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley. The argument holds that just as an artefact such as a watch implies the existence of an artisan, so the universe implies the existence of a divine creator. Here the analogy with the watch is not meant simply to illustrate a point. Rather, the analogy is supposed to show why we should conclude that the universe has a creator.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 일치: 'they serve simply to illustrate' — 유추가 설명 목적

❌ ② 일치: 'from the ancient Stoics to British theologian William Paley' — 고대 스토아~영국 신학자

❌ ③ 일치: 'a watch implies the existence of an artisan' — 시계→장인

✅ ④ 불일치: 'is not meant simply to illustrate a point' — 단순 설명이 아니라 핵심 논증. '오직 설명 목적'은 반대 ← 정답
det.tip: not meant simply to illustrate = 단순 설명이 아님. 오직 설명 목적이라는 것은 거짓

ch: 유추는 때로 단순히 요점을 설명하기 위해 사용된다.
